newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end on sharp gain after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end on sharp gain after U.S. data.

text.p: The CAC-40 index stormed higher to close firmly above the psychological 2,400 level on Monday, as benign U.S. economic indicators encouraged buying of French assets, traders said. It was the historic closing high for the index.

The market was already well supported on bullish profit expectations and low rates for 1997. When U.S. inflation and retail sales data was reported in line with expectations a buying spree in bonds and equities was triggered.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 40.87 points or 1.73 percent at 2,402.14, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 38.5 at 2,406 from 2,367.5 on Monday's close.

"The bond market is very strong, the dollar is rising sharply, the U.S. figures were in line with expectations - all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds," said EIFB analyst Pierre Vignaud.

Takeover and merger speculation excited trading in Cie Bancaire, a unit of Paribas, with shares in the finance house up 4.53 percent to 646 francs. Paribas' planned sale of Credit du Nord boosted its stock last week.
Another financial stock, Credit National, up 2.75 percent at 358.4, also attracted merger and acquisition talk.

Havas climbed 5.36 percent to 393 francs after shares in its CEP Communications unit were suspended, prompting speculation Havas might be preparing a buy out offer for minority shareholders. Alternatively, CEP may be preparing a big acquisition, traders said.

Rhone-Poulenc racked up a 5.82 percent gain to 176.3 francs, on the back of a Reuter report it would post profit growth of 20-25 percent and continuing merger speculation for the pharmaceuticals sector.
Total , another index heavyweight, shot up 4.78 percent after PaineWebber gave the stock a positive note.
Saint-Louis rose 3.17 percent to 1,369 francs, after it bought 15 percent stake in Spain's Ebro Agricolas, prompting Dresdner Kleinwort Benson to consider an upgrade.
